title: Filesystem & App Data Directories
objectives: Separate user data from sandbox temp space
Never expose raw fs APIs to the webview
body:
# Filesystem & App Data

## Where files belong

```rust
use tauri::Manager;
let dir = app.path().app_data_dir()?;          // %APPDATA%/<identifier>
std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
let db_path = dir.join("rust-mastery.db");     // this app's database
```

Per-user, per-app, OS-blessed. Config → same dir or config_dir(); caches →
cache_dir(); anything regenerable → temp.

**Student code never touches these paths.** Sandboxes live under
`env::temp_dir()/rust-mastery-sandbox/<uuid>/` — disposable, wiped by drop
guards. Two filesystem zones, zero overlap.

## Least privilege for the webview

This app ships NO fs plugin capability (`capabilities/default.json` grants only
`core:default`). File access flows exclusively through validated commands:
`save_editor_state`, `run_cargo_test(path within roots)`, …

Exposing `fs::read/write` plugins to the UI would hand XSS-equivalents the
whole disk. Commands + validation keep the blast radius to intended shapes.

## Path containment discipline

```rust
fn ensure_within(candidate: &Path, root: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, ()> {
    let normalized = normalize_lexical(candidate);   // collapse '..'
    if normalized.starts_with(root) { Ok(normalized) } else { Err(()) }
}
```

`run_cargo_test` applies exactly this before spawning cargo — see
`src-tauri/src/execution/validator.rs` with its traversal tests.
